note: What tools/restructure took out of which file, in order. Written by `extract`, read by `verify` and by server/test/engine-source.mjs. Do not edit by hand.

server/server.js.about: Small pieces every weather provider's answer is turned into: how many days, the condition groups with their words, compass points, clock and date parts.
Turns a wttr.in answer into the forecast shape the weather tile draws.
Turns an Open-Meteo answer into the forecast shape the weather tile draws.
Turns a met.no answer into the forecast shape the weather tile draws, with the feels-like temperature and the sun times met.no does not give.
Cleans a typed city and picks the place a weather search meant.
The services asked where this PC is when no city is set, and the check of what they answer.
The weather sources and the order they are tried in.
The dashboard a new install starts with, and the ids, sizes and grid limits a saved layout is checked against.
Checks of single saved values that many settings share: a number kept inside its range, a hex colour.
Checks the saved top bar settings: the side rails, the clock island and the order of the buttons.
Makes usable what the media hosts hand over: a cover that arrived broken, an artist and album packed into one field.
Checks the saved settings of notifications, calls and the paired phone.
Checks the saved browser tiles and the browser and app favourites.
Wraps raw sound samples in a WAV header, so any player or speech service can read them.
Measures how loud raw sound samples are: over the whole clip, at its loudest moment, and in decibels.
Starts the program that plays a WAV file on this operating system, without needing a window in focus.
Gets JSON back from PowerShell: out of the text a script printed, or from a file a script wrote.
Runs a program and gives back what it printed as a promise, with the output kept on the error when it fails.
Starts an application on Linux, where opening a program file with the desktop's "open" would show it as a document.
Shows a file in the file manager of this operating system, selected where the system can do that.
Tells whether a path points at another computer on the network, which Windows would sign in to just by touching it.
Reads a JSON file that must hold a plain object, and answers an empty one when it is missing or damaged.
What may be uploaded: the largest size and the accepted file types for backgrounds, fonts, tile pictures and slideshow pictures.
Reads the body of a request, as text or as bytes, and refuses one that grows past its limit.
Takes the one uploaded file out of a multipart form body, with its name and type.
Limits of the live event streams to the dashboards: unsent data per stream, and streams per device.
Small checks used when looking for ffmpeg: finding a file by name under a folder, and recognising the "not installed" error.
Facts about the settings file on disk: the shape of its identity, and the read errors that only mean "busy, try again".
Settings the dashboard owns and the engine only stores: kept when they are plain objects of a sane size.
Checks the saved choice of the screen Xenon runs on, and finds it in settings saved under its old name.
A calendar day in the user's own time zone, as the count of days Xenon was used stores it.
Checks the saved settings of Bit: which AI features are on, the proactive messages and the wake word.
Limits of Bit: the size of a message, the length of a live voice session, and what a look at the screen usually costs.
The fixed lists the Vitals settings are checked against: the meters, their defaults and the steps of the pet's reaction.
What the screensaver settings may hold: the idle times offered and the shapes of a scene reference.
What the background settings may hold: the built-in styles, the limits of a pasted picture or drawing code, and the lowest panel opacity.
Checks the saved custom font: only a font file the engine itself stored is kept.
Checks the saved settings of file search: the extra folders, the shortcut and what the results show.
Checks the saved keyboard shortcuts that switch the dashboard to a page.
Checks the saved settings of the Disk widget: the development folders and the age of old installers.
Checks the saved settings of the scrolling ticker bar: where it sits, how fast it moves and what feeds it.
Elgato Wave Link: the check of its saved settings, and the state widgets get while it is switched off.
Checks a saved list of Discord ids: digits only, no repeats, no longer than its limit.
Checks the saved settings of the PC numbers: the names given to fans and how often sensors are read.
Checks the saved state of the first-run guide.
Checks the saved choice to keep a history of game sessions.
Checks the saved settings of the Claude Code widget: which of its cards show outside the tile.
Checks the saved settings of the Codex widget: which of its cards show outside the tile.
Checks the saved lighting settings piece by piece: styles, palette, animation, providers and the reaction to an event.
The pairing tokens of light bridges inside the settings: blanked before settings go to a browser, and found when a backup needs to know.
Says which services of a configuration need a secret, so a restored backup can list the ones to set up again.
The folder files from a phone are saved in: kept out of the settings sent to a browser, and kept on disk when the browser saves.
Keeps secrets out of the settings sent to a browser, and puts them back when the browser saves settings without them.
Limits of file transfer from a phone: the free disk space that must remain, and the largest picture shown as a preview.
How long weather answers are reused, and how long to wait after the place could not be found.
What the weather settings may hold: the languages a forecast can come in and the fields that can be shown or hidden.
The small steps of checking a saved dashboard layout: one tile, the order of tiles, the tabs and the number of pages.
Converts a layout saved on the old 12-column grid to the units of the 24-column grid.
Finds which uploaded tile pictures a layout still uses, and says how long an unused one is kept before it is deleted.
Finds which uploaded slideshow pictures the settings still use.
Packs one picture of a streamed screen or browser tile with its description into a single binary message.
The example widgets that ship with Xenon and can be installed by name.
The shape every note and timer id must have, because ids end up inside the page.
Gives each saved list a number higher than the last one, so a screen can tell the newer of two copies.
Notes as the engine stores them: their limits, the check of saved or received notes, and the conversion to and from plain text.
Tasks as the engine stores them: their limit, the check of one task and of the list, and the fields a dashboard may edit.
Calendar events as the engine stores them: the check of the saved list, the fields a dashboard may edit, and the colours of subscribed calendars.
Timers and stopwatches: how many there may be, the two kinds, a new id, and the seconds counted or left.
Builds the short sounds of timers, reminders and notifications from a list of notes.
